restoration_note: Teaching 53 describes the First Man going forth against the Enemy in five garments — the living fire (= divine love) within four helper-garments (wind, water, light, air). Love alone does the work of quenching the self, but takes a wound; the four helpers also suffer. The air-garment in particular is stripped naked and replaced with a living-air garment so the four can hold together as 'the spirit of life.' The second half (ch.52) contrasts the concord of the Lord's principles — none transgressing the commandment given by another — with the self, who is 'one of a single practice, herself alone.' Most letter-level restorations were editor-supplied and are confirmed by parallels within the teaching (ⲡⲉϩϩⲧⲁⲩ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁⲛ in line 22, ⲥⲱⲃⲣⲙⲩⲥⲧⲏⲣⲓⲟⲛ in line 15, ⲡⲁⲣⲁⲃⲁ ⲛ̄ⲧⲉⲛⲧⲟⲗⲏ in line 2). The substantial lacuna at gap {22} is constrained by the five-garment theme to ϯⲟⲩ. Gap {42} is fixed by the formula 'spirit of life' (ⲡⲛⲉⲩⲙⲁ ⲛ̄ⲱⲛⲍ). Gaps {43}-{45} are constrained by the ch.52 vocabulary parallel to lines 1-2 (commandment + practice). Sections 3122-3124 are too damaged to restore and are honestly left unrestored. Several mid-line gaps in ch.51.16-17 ({30},{32}-{35}) and ch.52.5 ({46}-{49}) carry only low confidence proposals.
